root_cause.text: The ublk control path lacked state validation in `UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE`, causing `ublk_ctrl_set_size()` in `drivers/block/ublk_drv.c` to dereference the `struct ublk_device` field `ub->ub_disk` even when it is NULL before start or after stop.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states `ublk_ctrl_set_size() unconditionally dereferences ub->ub_disk via set_capacity_and_notify() without checking if it is NULL`, notes that `ub->ub_disk is NULL before UBLK_CMD_START_DEV completes` and `after UBLK_CMD_STOP_DEV runs`, and the patch adds `if (!ub->ub_disk) { ret = -ENODEV; goto out; }` under `ub->mutex` and changes the handler to return that error.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The ublk control path lacked state validation in `UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE`, causing `ublk_ctrl_set_size()` in `drivers/block/ublk_drv.c` to dereference the `struct ublk_device` field `ub->ub_disk` even when it is NULL before start or after stop.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states `ublk_ctrl_set_size() unconditionally dereferences ub->ub_disk via set_capacity_and_notify() without checking if it is NULL`, notes that `ub->ub_disk is NULL before UBLK_CMD_START_DEV completes` and `after UBLK_CMD_STOP_DEV runs`, and the patch adds `if (!ub->ub_disk) { ret = -ENODEV; goto out; }` under `ub->mutex` and changes the handler to return that error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a disk-existence check to ublk_ctrl_set_size so resizing fails with -ENODEV instead of accessing a missing ub_disk.
intent_record.what: The function ublk_ctrl_set_size was changed from returning void to returning int, a local ret variable initialized to 0 was added, a check for !ub->ub_disk was inserted under the mutex, that check sets ret to -ENODEV and jumps to a new out label, and the function now unlocks the mutex at out and returns ret after calling set_capacity_and_notify only when ub->ub_disk exists.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the size-setting path now detects when the device has no associated disk object and avoids dereferencing ub->ub_disk, returning -ENODEV instead of proceeding. This prevents invalid access while preserving the normal behavior of updating dev_sectors and notifying capacity changes when the disk is present.

intent_record.intent_summary: Propagate ublk_ctrl_set_size() errors in the update-size command handler instead of always returning success.
intent_record.what: In the UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE case of ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd(), the code was changed from calling ublk_ctrl_set_size(ub, &header) and then unconditionally setting ret = 0, to directly assigning its return value with ret = ublk_ctrl_set_size(ub, &header).
intent_record.how: This makes the command handler propagate the success or failure result from ublk_ctrl_set_size() instead of always reporting success, allowing runtime errors during size update to be returned to the caller.

grouping_result.intent: Add a disk-existence check to ublk_ctrl_set_size so resizing fails with -ENODEV instead of accessing a missing ub_disk.
Propagate ublk_ctrl_set_size() errors in the update-size command handler instead of always returning success.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds the missing state validation in `ublk_ctrl_set_size()` by checking whether `ub->ub_disk` exists before resizing, preventing the NULL dereference described in the root cause.

The change affects the UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE handler for the same path as the root cause. By propagating ublk_ctrl_set_size() errors instead of always succeeding, it is directly tied to handling failure conditions in the vulnerable update-size control path.

candidates.rationale: This directly dereferences ub->ub_disk without validating that the disk exists, which is the root cause of the NULL dereference before start or after stop.
This updates device size state even when the device may not have a valid ub_disk, contributing to the missing state validation in the update-size control path.
This invokes the vulnerable resize helper from UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE without ensuring the device is in a valid started state, exposing the NULL dereference path.
This forces success for the update-size command and prevents reporting any invalid state, reflecting the missing validation/error propagation in the vulnerable path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly dereferences ub->ub_disk in the update-size path without validating that the disk exists. When UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE is issued before start or after stop, ub->ub_disk can be NULL, causing the reported NULL dereference.

This statement invokes the vulnerable resize helper from the UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE control path without checking whether the device is in a valid started state, thereby exposing the NULL dereference in ublk_ctrl_set_size().

commit 98b995660bff011d8e00af03abd74ac7d1ac1390
Author: Omri Mann <omri@nvidia.com>
Date:   Mon Apr 21 13:59:50 2025 +0300

    ublk: Add UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE
    
    Currently ublk only allows the size of the ublkb block device to be
    set via UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS before UBLK_CMD_START_DEV is triggered.
    
    This does not provide support for extendable user-space block devices

    causing IO interruption.
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows both the newly added handler and the full body of the new helper `ublk_ctrl_set_size()`, as well as the dispatch path that invokes it. The vulnerable construct is present in `ublk_ctrl_set_size(struct ublk_device *ub, ...)`: it does `set_capacity_and_notify(ub->ub_disk, p->dev_sectors);` after only taking `ub->mutex` and updating `p->dev_sectors`, but there is no validation that `ub->ub_disk` is non-NULL or that the device is in a started/running state. This matches the root cause: `UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE` can reach code that dereferences `ub->ub_disk` even before start or after stop. The command is newly wired into the control path in `ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd()` via `case UBLK_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE: ublk_ctrl_set_size(ub, header); ret = 0; break;`, and there is likewise no state check there either. Therefore the vulnerable logic is introduced by this commit. No fix is present, because there is no guard such as a state validation or `if (!ub->ub_disk) ...` before calling `set_capacity_and_notify()`.
